players.product: EUV / ArF photoresists, CMP slurries and polyimides

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Higuchi: Q1 of the fiscal year ending March 2027 revenue was JPY826.5 billion, a record high for a Q1, driven by Healthcare (particularly endoscopes) and Electronics (Semiconductor Materials such as CMP slurry, and data tapes) plus FX; operating income was JPY51.2 billion versus an internal plan of approximately JPY52.0 billion to JPY53.0 billion, declining on higher Bio CDMO fixed costs, one-time Business Innovation expenses and higher raw material costs; net income attributable to FUJIFILM Holdings JPY37.4 billion
quarterly_data.figure: revenue JPY826.5 billion; operating income JPY51.2 billion; net income JPY37.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Higuchi: full-year revenue forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 raised by JPY90.0 billion to JPY3,560.0 billion on stronger Electronics sales and FX; operating income forecast maintained at JPY365.0 billion (including an approximately JPY6.0 billion positive impact from U.S. tariff refunds), with the Healthcare forecast lowered for a slower Bio CDMO profit ramp-up and Electronics and Business Innovation raised; the company continues to forecast record revenue, operating income and net income
quarterly_data.figure: revenue forecast JPY3,560.0 billion (raised by JPY90.0 billion); operating income forecast JPY365.0 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Higuchi: Electronics segment Q1 revenue rose 25% YoY to JPY127.7 billion, driven by Semiconductor Materials including copper interconnect CMP slurry and NTI developer and other advanced-node materials used for generative AI applications, and by AF materials on higher data tape sales to major IT companies; operating income rose 38.2% YoY to JPY31.1 billion; Electronics exceeded the internal plan by more than JPY8.0 billion
quarterly_data.figure: Electronics revenue JPY127.7 billion (+25%); operating income JPY31.1 billion (+38.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Iwasaki (GM, Electronic Materials): Semiconductor Materials revenue grew 31% YoY in Q1, or about 20% excluding FX; the company reviews the outlook while exchanging three-year forecasts with major semiconductor manufacturers and believes the underlying demand trend is unlikely to change significantly; demand strengthens as nodes advance, AI-related semiconductor demand including in Taiwan and South Korea remains robust and demand for Intel CPUs is beginning to improve; he does not expect the full year to simply be four times Q1, with external risks such as the Middle East built into the plan
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor Materials revenue +31% YoY (about 20% excluding FX)

quarterly_data.signal: Iwasaki (GM, Electronic Materials): in back-end processes the main product, ZEMATES polyimide materials, delivered very strong growth in Q1 with demand increasing in Q2 and beyond; the company supplies insulating materials for interposers and encapsulation, and while panel-level packaging has not entered full-scale production, major semiconductor manufacturers and OSATs are in the final stages of evaluating its polyimide films, which already contribute revenue at the prototype stage; polyimide materials for build-up substrates are in development with positive customer evaluations

Iwasaki (GM, Electronic Materials): the company's CMP slurry for back-end stacking processes is already on the market and has been adopted by a Korean manufacturer for NAND applications, with use expected to expand into DRAM; thermal-management materials will also begin contributing to revenue; the original FY2030 revenue target of JPY500.0 billion did not fully reflect back-end materials, and strong growth in polyimide buffer coats and insulating materials suggests the target can be achieved ahead of schedule
quarterly_data.figure: FY2030 revenue target JPY500.0 billion (expected ahead of schedule)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Higuchi: the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake caused no major damage to production equipment at the Display Materials and Semiconductor Materials manufacturing site in Kikuyo, Kumamoto; production resumed in stages from August 2 after safety checks and inspections; some delays in customer deliveries are expected for certain products, but the overall impact on performance is expected to be limited at this stage

CFO Higuchi: price increases have spread beyond semiconductor memory to IT-related components such as PCs and servers, with further recent increases and longer procurement lead times; the company has factored in an additional JPY14.0 billion of costs on top of the previous JPY11.0 billion, for an expected full-year cost increase of JPY25.0 billion, and will pursue pricing and alternative procurement; Imaging GM Igarashi: the DRAM needed has been secured but prices have risen more than expected, and the Imaging outlook reflects these procurement risks and announced price increases
quarterly_data.figure: full-year memory and IT component cost increase JPY25.0 billion (previous JPY11.0 billion + additional JPY14.0 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Higuchi: global demand for data-center capacity remains extremely strong and data tape is gaining attention as a highly secure long-term archiving solution; part of the demand reflects the current tight supply of memory chips, but the more structural driver is that customers no longer want to rely solely on semiconductor memory or disk-based storage for archiving and are adopting tape for its higher security and better energy efficiency

Bio CDMO GM Iida: the Q1 Bio CDMO operating loss was in the high JPY20.0 billion range, approximately JPY10.0 billion below the internal plan; the full-year Healthcare forecast now includes a downward revision of more than JPY30.0 billion, and Iida confirmed the full-year Bio CDMO loss is around JPY70.0 billion (previous outlook just under JPY40.0 billion); the majority of the downside comes from the small-to-mid-scale North Carolina site (antibody projects), with the large-scale North Carolina site just under JPY10.0 billion and Denmark broadly in line; no FY2027 operating income figure can be given yet
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 loss in the high JPY20.0 billion range; full-year Bio CDMO loss around JPY70.0 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Bio CDMO GM Iida: at the small-to-mid-scale North Carolina site the FDA conducted an unannounced inspection; the company voluntarily suspended operations site-wide, is supplying corrective actions and data, expects no equipment issues, and aims to resume operations during Q2; at the large-scale North Carolina site technology transfer is complete and long-term customer contracts remain in place, but batch cadence is slower than planned, with ramp-up expected to accelerate toward H2; early-stage orders, notably antibody projects, are soft, and the Toyama site will be its first facility to perform ADC conjugation, offering full-service ADC capability

CFO Higuchi and FUJIFILM Business Innovation President Hama: the company will begin evaluating strategic options for the Business Innovation segment, including a partial spin-off with a view to implementing it in two to three years, after which FUJIFILM Holdings would retain less than a 20% stake; Business Innovation posted a Q1 operating loss of JPY1.4 billion partly because tight server availability delayed server installations and deferred service revenues (timing, not lost business); it plans a 10% price increase from September, expects structural reforms to yield around JPY10.0 billion of benefits next year, targets a 10% operating margin in FY2030 and expects to return to profit for the full year
quarterly_data.figure: Business Innovation Q1 operating loss JPY1.4 billion; around JPY10.0 billion reform benefits next year; 10% price increase from September
